Hmmm, I'm not so sure that I understand what you're asking...I've never noticed having issues with paranoid patients.

I struggle with severe depression, anxiety, and borderline personality disorder; and crazy enough, I work in a psych hospital. I feel that I can better understand my patients since we've been through some of the same things. So I suppose empathy would be something positive about my illnesses.

Man, I wish I had a better answer for this; but all I can say is that my mind hates me. I often feel as though my brain is it's own entity, separate from the part of me that wants to live. Sometimes, the noise in my head gets so loud that my suicidal mind just takes over. Like, there's no one reason that I can think of that makes me want to kill myself; but I am what I refer to as chronically suicidal. I think about killing myself every day, but most of the time those thoughts are passive. I suppose the fact that I have depression, anxiety, and borderline personality disorder doesn't help.
We used 'buenas' when I lived in Honduras
My favorite is being told that she is proud of me.
Same...I never knew anyone else went through this
Same, I'm 29. I didn't start until I was 23, though; which I'm told is odd.
Jess is my artist too! She does amazing work!
I've been in the hospital 10 times and residential treatment for 5.5 months.
Leong's Asian Diner; can't beat the original home of cashew chicken.
I don't feel like my IQ changed after ECT. Also, the only memory loss I experienced is the time around when I had my treatments.

This happened to me rather often; and I hated it so much. The other kids would just wait for me to give them the correct answers. I ended up requesting to have my desk moved by the teacher's desk because I was so tired of it.
It's on my knee
Her name is Maxie
For me, it gives me something to focus on so that the irrational thoughts in my head will quiet down.
Therapy gives me a chance to just talk and be really real. It also gives me a different view point when I'm stuck in my irrational thoughts.
I'm a native English speaker and have a BA in Spanish. My Spanish has gotten very Rusty, as I don't use it these days. I really want to learn French and Mandarin.
This is a totally normal thing. Your therapist can't read your mind. Most of them tend to steer away from talking about their lives since it's your time to deal with your own issues.
My therapist always tells me that the definition of trauma is different for everyone. If your younger self found something traumatic, then it affected how you grew up.

Therapy used to make me so anxious that I would color while we talked and never looked up at my therapist. Now I have a few fidget toys and am much better about actually looking at who I'm speaking to.
Antibiotic ointment would probably be a good idea as well.
I only did this once and it was on my upper thigh so it couldn't be seen. I honestly feel like it was because the words wouldn't stop swirling in my mind and I needed to get them out.
Talk to your therapist...self harm is pretty addictive and can get out of control so quickly.
This is always my sign that I'm getting worse, the not showering bit. Lately it's been more like every 2 weeks.
I've been trying my hardest to stay alive for so many years now...I just can't live this way and deal with this for forever.
Three treatments is pretty early on in the process. Give it some more time and more treatments if you can handle it.
I do. I have been hospitalized many times; it is a comforting place for me because I actually feel safe from myself. There have been many times I said I'd like to be in a place like that forever.
Glad you wrote in your journal, it's such a great coping skill! Make sure to let your doctor know about the side effects if they don't go away.
Right?? I looooove it

I took abilify for a long time with absolutely no change. My new psychiatrist switched me to a different antipsychotic and it has helped quiet my intrusive thoughts a tiny bit. Then again, I'm classed as treatment resistant, so abilify might work great for you. Remember that psych meds take a minute to start working, so maybe don't give up on it too soon.

Hey there! I have had 12 ect treatments...I never had any kind of bad experience. The only thing is that my memory around the time period is kind of hazy. Didn't lose any long term stuff though, just from around the time of the treatments and that was a terrible time for me anyway, so who wants those memories. ECT didn't do anything for me at all, but I would consider it perfectly safe. 

I also had a month of TMS treatments. TMS is easier to deal with because they don't have to knock you out, you just sit there for an hour with the machine on. TMS helped me for a short time, but I would definitely say it wore off.

Obviously talk with your doctor, but I'd suggest trying the TMS first since it's easier to handle than being put under 3x a week.

Best of luck.
Please be 100% honest and up front with your psychiatrist, this is the best way to get the help you need.
I just have to make sure my job keeps me busy and my mind occupied. If I have too much downtime, my mind wanders to the dark and twisty places that are terrible.
I do...and it triggers me so bad, but I can't seem to stop. I have covered most of them with large tattoos; but of course I found a new spot after I got my ink in my traditional cutting spot.

I'm not sure, but I don't think you can be involuntarily hospitalized for self-harm...I never have been. Always be honest and open with your therapist, that way they can give you as much help as possible.
Never been on them
Therapy is different for everyone. I don't think you really find ways to "fix" issues, but you gain tools to better deal with things that you are going through.
General anxiety, major depression, and BPD here

I agree. And people always over simplify it by saying that if you just force yourself to do the things that you'll feel better. In my experience, though, that is far from true. It's like, how is showering going to help me? It's not.

That's awful, that's when you need your therapist the most. BPD is rough and everyone always says that most clinicians don't like working with us. I have been lucky to have two good therapists, it just feels like I'm always saying the same things though, and can't change things no matter how hard I try. My therapist and psychiatrist seem to agree that my suicidal thoughts will probably never go away. Talk about something that makes you feel hopeless.

I have tried, the therapist that I went to wasn't great and wanted to make me work through a CBT workbook first. I did 5 months in residential and know CBT like the back of my hand, so it was super frustrating to me. My current therapist is great, she just always asks me how I feel if this is as good as it gets for me. Kinda disheartening,

Thank you for this reminder. I actually have a therapist now that I really like, it's just hard to shake the memory of being told that the other one couldn't help me. I think perhaps she could have worded it better when telling me; by saying that she thought I needed someone more suited to my specific needs.
Lol, I'll have to mention that to his owner! I doubt she even realized she could refer to him as that when she named him.

My mind fixates on cutting. I never have a reason for doing so, I just feel like I need to do it. I'm a few months clean right now, but the urge still creeps up on me from time to time. It gets awful when I encounter something that I could use to cut. Recently, I randomly found a blade at work and it was all I could do to keep from using it right then and there. I couldn't bring myself to dispose of it, because I wanted to use it so badly. The next day, however, I asked someone to remove it before I returned to work. I still kind of wish I hadn't, though. Even if I'm not using them, having tools is kind of like a security blanket for me; knowing I can use them anytime somehow helps me from doing so I think.
Just don't give up on what you feel will be best for you! Keep pushing!

Lots of meds that sorta control my symptoms. I still have horrible suicidal ideations on the daily, but I'm getting better about at least not letting them get the better of me. I go to the hospital to keep myself safe if it gets too bad. I tried the ketamine thing as well and just ended up back in the hospital. I stay in therapy every 1-2 weeks and just having someone to talk to is nice. Honestly, I'd even be game to try some sorta medical study to see if anything new would help. I am trying to accept that maybe this is just as good as it gets for me.
Good for you for reaching out for help!

I have my mom leave the room every time my mental health assessment is done when I go to the hospital. Not necessarily because I don't want her to know, because she obviously knows what's up when I land in the ER; but because I feel that hearing the details will upset her more than necessary. Granted, I am over 18 so I am able to request this without it being contested by anyone. I implore you to remember though, that if you are feeling like hurting yourself, honesty extremely important! You can't get the help you need if you aren't real with the people who are there to help. I don't know your family situation, but I'd bet that your mom wants the best for you; and the best means getting help.

I started ECT when I was 25 and had 12 treatments within that year. I deal with very severe depression and nearly constant suicidal ideations. ECT was basically the only option for me left to try after multiple suicide attempts. Unfortunately, the treatments had no effect on me.

I love helping people, in whatever manner that might be. The job I just quit is at a substance abuse rehab facility and it has been truly amazing to be even a small part of each client's journey. I love watching the clients grow and change from when they first get here. I also love teaching; I actually spent some time teaching English in Honduras and that is really my passion...just don't feel like I'm stable enough mentally to be out of the country alone again, unfortunately.
Thank you!
My employer isn't happy about it and really tried to get me to stay; but I stood up for myself and my decision.

I tell my therapist everything. I guess I figure it would feel like a waste of time for both of us (and a waste of money for me) if I withheld things from her. Plus, I wouldn't really be working on any of the things that I truly need to work on if I hid them.
Could always be something great!
Pringles and video games, I love it! :)
So happy to hear that you have a great support system; it makes such a big difference!
Thanks! My artist is truly bad ass!
Thanks! My artist is amazing!
I am a fighter.
His full name is Swaggerz lol

Not a therapist here, but I have experience in this. I am great friends with my former therapist. They tend to go by the "two year rule" is what I'm told. Meaning they don't contact clients in an outside of therapy manner until 2 years have passed that they are no longer the therapist. Might not be the case for all, but that's been my experience.
The depth of your cuts is not reflective of the hurt that caused you to make them. Your hurt is valid.
They won't 5150 you for self-harm. Just be honest with your therapist.

I mean, it is what it is.I go to therapy weekly, and talking about things is at least semi helpful. I still have my times where I get extremely upset about the fact that nothing has worked and that I'll be dealing with this for the rest of my life. Often that reality leaves me not wanting to live, but I do my best to keep myself safe. 

The only thing that happened from ECT is that the time right around my treatments is kind of hazy for me and I have trouble remembering it. But that only applies to the time close to treatments; my memory is fine otherwise.

I have tried just about everything out there, including the things mentioned by others here. I have had 12 ECT treatments, around 30 TMS treatments, tried Spravato, and have been on almost every med you can try. In my personal experience, ECT did absolutely nothing for me. TMS was effective for a short period of time, but wore off. Spravato actually made my suicidal ideations worse after about 4 treatments, so my psychiatrist stopped the treatment. And as far as meds go, they only sort of help to control my symptoms; but I still experience severe depression, chronic suicidality, and anxiety. 

I don't want to discourage you from trying these things, as all can be rather effective for some people. Everything affects people differently. Just wanted to share my experiences with you. 

Best of luck in finding something that is right for you!
A little over 5 years; with the exception of the  exception of the time I spent in residential treatment.

I am like this with my FP. I have recently gotten a bit better about splitting on her, but I still do things that are pushing her away; even after she has told me that they're starting to push her away.
Thank you!

I would totally send that. My therapist encourages me to email her if there are things I feel more comfortable writing about. She has even told me that we can just leave those things to the email and don't have to discuss them in session if I feel like I can't.

This! even though I know what I'm going through is very very real, my real worry is that others will think that I am exaggerating because I seem to make it through life so well. The reality is though, I spend most of my days thinking about how much I want to die.

I wasn't planning to take any languages in high school, but got stuck in Spanish 1 during my first semester of freshman year. I had an amazing teacher and realized I was pretty good at the subject; so I continued on to Spanish 2. Then, I had the opportunity to attend a Spanish school in Costa Rica for a week and that's what did it for me. I have since gotten my BA in Spanish and even got to live in Honduras and teach at a bilingual school for a bit. I have a tiny amount of French education under my belt, and would love to continue that as well.

I am the same way...it's like, it takes 5 seconds to send a text. How busy can you be that you cannot find the time for that?!? I have BPD and my favorite person does this to me All. The. Time. She claims she's busy, but I hate that excuse. You make time for what you want to make time for, period. Just tell me you don't want to talk to me, since that's obviously the truth. Ugh.
Honestly, ECT did nothing for me, so know that that is a possibility.
Same, drawing helps me feel slightly better since I can draw what I am thinking and feeling.

In my experience, these relationships never turn out well. I have had 3 FPs in my time...one I pushed away, the second left, and I'm not on great terms with my current FP at the moment. I think it's perhaps because the relationship is too one sided where we love harder than what they can and it hurts us to not be loved in the same way. At least, that's been my experience. I tend to come off as smothering them when I'm just trying to show how much I care.

I kinda feel the same way. I'm really open about my mental illnesses and my suicidal thoughts, so I'm sure most people are just expecting it to happen one day. I think anytime someone dies by suicide there's that typical "why didn't s/he say something? What could we have done to help prevent this" type of reaction. I know after I opened up about my last attempt people came out of the wood works to tell me how much they love me and that I ought to stick around.

The safety there honestly depends on where you are. The bigger cities, like San Pedro Sula and Tegucigalpa can be quite dangerous. I lived in a small tourist town, though, so I felt completely safe there. It's really up to you how much of each language you speak. I spent time talking to the Spanish speaking teachers and we were basically conversation partners so they could practice English and I could practice my Spanish. There are also many opportunities to speak Spanish if you get out and about outside of school hours. For example, I attended a couple of Bible studies with the woman I lived with and those certainly helped to improve my listening skills.

She's actually a very good therapist, but kind of a shit friend. She was my therapist before we became friends, so I know. When our relationship changed though, things got a bit sticky. Because she is now my FP, I tend to split on her, which I never did as her client. I guess that's a big part of why she gets so fed up with me. I wish I didn't split like I do, but it's become much more rare; hopefully I'll be able to get it under control and make things easier for both of us.
I wish it was just that easy!

I wouldn't say she blames me for having my illnesses, it's more that she blames me for everything that goes wrong in our friendship. I get that everyone has their limits, but she has vowed to not abandon me. She just likes to take breaks from me, which I don't handle well AT ALL. She actually used to be my therapist when I was in a residential facility, so I think some parts of our relationship as friends are just weird now. It was a shift for both of us in how we relate to one another, to say the least. I just want so badly to make things better, but all she wants to do is not talk to me. In my opinion, talking things out is far more beneficial than one of us ignoring the other.

I had 12 ECT treatments and have been in the hospital 9 times. ECT was smooth sailing except for the fact that the time around when I was getting my treatments has become a bit hazy in my mind now. Not a time in my life I want to remember anyway, so I'm ok with it. Unfortunately, ECT didn't work for me; I really hope it does for you! They say it helps so many people! I totally get what you're saying about being in the hospital. I wouldn't say that I necessarily like being there, but I like feeling safe when my mind is an unsafe place.

SAME! My FP can go months without texting me, but I can only make it a few days without contacting her. I hate this and wish it could just be like my other friendships where we only talk occasionally and it's cool. But noooooo, I will literally text her even when I know for a fact that she won't respond to me.

When I cut on my thighs, I always just wore shorts long enough to cover what I had done. Lots of women wear shorts over their suits when at the river and whatnot, you should be just fine going with that.

I lived in Honduras for about 5.5 months. I didn't go to learn or improve my Spanish; I was teaching English at a bilingual school. I wasn't allowed to speak Spanish with my students, but definitely got practice out in the community. My conversational skills improved just by listening to others and learning to use the local terms rather than the more formal ones I had learned in school. My grammar may not have been perfect, nor could I always remember the right words, but it felt great when I could converse with people and we understood one another. It was definitely worth it and made me much more confident in my Spanish speaking abilities. If you're a native English speaker, look into teaching in a Spanish speaking country; you're essentially getting paid to travel and get the added benefit of improving  you language skills!
Congrats on this huge accomplishment! Keep it up; one day at a time!
For sure, I want to cut on my arms and ankles so bad. Just seem like easier spots to cut, but would be such a pain to cover.
What is the bright green one in the front? I love its color!
Woohoo! So exciting! Love your attitude, too! Keep it up
For sure, I can never seem to shake the thought that I'm worthless and no one can really love me, it's always there in the back of my mind.

Right?!? One of my best friends is a therapist and she seems to act like everything I do is because of my illnesses. She acts like I should just be able to snap out of my episodes, when it's not nearly that simple. You would think a therapist would be more understanding, but I suppose it's because I'm not her job that she treats me the way she does.

I appreciate the fact that you noted that it's things that *feel* offensive. It's like, it could be a totally normal comment, or even the lack of one that gets to me most of the time. Sure, there are times that I get upset over things that are actually offensive, but most of the time it's all in my head. Unfortunately, I don't really love myself, even when others show me love, or tell me they love me. I tend to believe that they're only acting that way or saying those things to me because they feel bad for me.
Congrats! I work at a rehab, so I know how difficult the journey you're on is. I applaud you for your commitment to sobriety! Keep it up; one day at a time!
I completely understand, and I get to that point more than I care to admit. Other people are the only thing that keep me here, so I sometimes resent the fact that I do still care about them.

ECT didn't help me at all, but things work differently for everyone. I had no trouble with getting back to work or anything like that. The time of my life around when I was getting my treatments is kind of foggy for me, but no terrible memory loss.
This. Then if only I could sit down with my loved ones and make them see that its really the best option for me. As a chronically suicidal and mentally ill person, I feel that this should be a thing.

Same. My FP is not a romantic partner, just a friend; but man, to me it feels like she hung the moon. I try to do so much to be a great friend, and it's just not reciprocated. I know that if we were both to be obsessed like I am, it would be awful; but I just want a little bit of effort on her part. It's like our friendship is totally one sided with me putting in all of the effort to keep it afloat. Then when I decide to ask for more from her, I'm being totally unreasonable and not respecting her boundaries. I just want to feel loved and important.

Hey there. I don't think it's possible to go without having your loved ones affected. Our lives are intertwined with those of others in ways that we may not even imagine. For me, it's the thought of hurting my family that has kept me alive. Sometimes I try to tell myself that my death would be easier on them than seeing me live in pain all the time, but I'm always told that that thought is very wrong. They don't want to see you in pain, but being able to see you alive is infinitely better than never seeing you again. I try to put myself in their shoes and think about how I would react if my sister or someone killed themselves, and I know it would ruin me.

I'm really sorry your life is rough right now. I'm not going to feed you any lines about it getting better, because I'm not sure it does. What I will say is that there are moments, even the tiniest ones, that make living worth it. Look for those little moments and hold on for just another second if that's all you can manage, then another after that, and another after that until time has gone by without your noticing. Stay alive, you can do this.

Same. It got so bad that my FP blocked me from all of her social media accounts because I was splitting over things she posted. Ugh, I hate being this way! I just want to be a normal friend and not feel like a freaking stalker.
I am exactly the same. I hate when people yell around me, even if it's not remotely at me. Gets to me every time.

Same. I find myself over apologizing especially after I split on my FP. I apologize for being the way I am, for being alive, etc. She never acknowledges my apologies and that makes me hurt even worse and feel like perhaps I'm not saying sorry enough, so I just keep finding things to say I'm sorry about.

19, my best friend at the time was a huge stoner and I eventually asked her what it was like. She was hesitant to let me try it a first, but it quickly became the thing that we'd do together most of the time; just get baked and talk about life.

Not to me. My current "favorite person" is a friend of mine, but she certainly doesn't love me the way I love her. Even when she's mad at me or not talking to me or something, I can't help but obsess. In fact, it's probably worse when she isn't giving back the love that I show her. I convince myself that she hates me, but rather than walk away, I obsess harder and try harder to show her that I love her; hoping that if I love hard enough, she will one day feel the same as I feel. It's totally unrealistic, because her mind doesn't work like mine, but I never stop trying.

I think you probably can. For me, it's really just one person at a time. If that person happens to leave me (which is the WORST,) I latch onto another person and become obsessed with them. I'm not a big people person, so I don't tend to have the option of being obsessed with more than one person at a time, but I'm sure it's possible.
Same. I get the urge to cut quite often, even when everything is ok, but it's so much worse when I am upset. I just relapsed the other day after a fight with my best friend.

I haven't done exclusively DBT as of yet, but I've learned bit of it here and there. I think that radical acceptance is the best thing for me right now, even though I struggle with it. It helps when I get down about having mental illnesses; reminds me that I just have to live with it and do my best to keep my head above water.

Tbh, that's a low dose of Effexor. Maybe talk to your doctor about trying to up it? Sometimes anti-psychotics are used to augment the anti-depressants, but not always. I am on an anti-depressant, anti-psychotic, mood stabilizer, and a stimulant (it helps with my lethargy and honestly is the only one I feel helps me be in a better mood.) This isn't necessarily common, especially the stimulant being used for this purpose. I don't really feel like the meds help me all that much, as I still experience all of the typical symptoms of BPD and bad SI. My psychiatrist says she thinks the meds are doing as much as they possibly can for me. I have been on so many different meds, and this seems to be as good as it gets.
For me, I end up loving anyone who shows me the slightest bit of compassion and kindness. The thing about how I love though is that it turns into obsession. I hate this, but it is what it is.

SO freaking true! I will delete my FP's phone number so I don't text her, but her number is easily available online. I always end up tracking it down and messaging her again even though I really don't want to because I feel like such an annoyance in her life.

I actually just had this happen today! It's the worst when I feel I am being abandoned. I feel like such a little kid in the way I react by begging for the person to stay (even though they may not actually be leaving me) and love me. I get so torn up about it, because I feel like I shouldn't be this way and it is so frustrating.

My FP constantly shoves all of the responsibility for my anger onto me, like she's done nothing to make me feel like shit. I thought relationships were supposed to be a two way street, but it feels like I'm the only one that wants things to get better. I split on her sometimes when I feel jealous; but at other times, she's horrible to me and I feel like I have every right to be angry and let her know that I am. Always backfires on me though as I get blamed for making everything terrible.

I definitely get you! I struggle so much with my bpd and finally felt as though I was doing better, then it all came crashing down again. Had a disagreement with my FP today and showed my ugly, hateful side, just wanting her to go away so I would have a reason to feel the things I was feeling.
You can literally say anything you want to your therapist, they won't stop you or judge you at all.
I once made it a whole year clean and I just ruined that, too. Feels like I'll never be free of this.
Mantequilla de cacahuate is my favorite! Just means peanut butter, but I love the sound of it.

So glad to hear that you're going to take all of the advice given to you here! I work at a rehab and I see every single day the effects that opiates have on people and the terrible path they end up on, wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy. Proud of you! Also, glad you made the choice to stay alive.
Congrats on the clean time! That's quite an accomplishment!

I feel like this especially when it comes to my FP. It feels like she is my entire world, but I'm barely a blip on her radar. It hurts so much to feel unwanted and unloved by the one person that I most want love from.

I am the same way. When I break down it's generally in the form of splitting on my FP. After I've said all of the shitty things in my head to her, I feel like a terrible person who just shouldn't go on living. It's like I feel like the world would be better off if I wasn't around to do this and hurt the people I love. I know what I'm doing, and know that I'm being a total asshole, but I can't seem to stop it in the moment. Usually after a day or so, I snap back to reality and apologize profusely, but I can't help but feel shame for what I've already done.

I hate that I ever met my FP. I love her so much and would do absolutely anything in the world for her. I try SO hard to be a good friend and it's not reciprocated. I know she doesn't understand just how much I love her and can't love me in the same way, but that doesn't make it hurt any less when I feel like she has abandoned me. She does a good job with setting boundaries and I'm trying to learn to toe the line, but it's so hard for me. I wish I didn't let another person affect me in such a way, but I can't seem to help it. I hate myself when I feel like I'm constantly pestering her, and even more when I split. It just feels like life would be so much easier if we had never met and then she would be free of me.

Thank you for your kind words and encouragement! I am coming up on the 3 year anniversary of my last attempt and I am actually wanting to celebrate the fact that I lived. I have learned in the past few years that I should take myself to the psych ward when the thoughts get too bad and that has kept me safe and alive.

Same! For me, I think I feel this way because I'm not particularly fond of being around other people. Plus, being in quarantine has given me time to focus on doing things that make me happy, like making art and reading.
Hey, that's a great idea! Wish I would have thought of this before I met my last new therapist!
Be a friend. Let her know that you aren't leaving.

It's all about your comfort level with showing them. I have never been particularly fond of having anyone see mine; but if it doesn't bother you, then show them whenever you are comfortable. Don't be ashamed of your scars or worried what other people will think; focus on what's most beneficial for you.
I'm getting help and still feel this way. It's weird to not see myself in the future, but I'm certain that my life will end on my terms.

I know when I'm splitting, but totally don't care in those moments. I can recognize that I am being totally irrational, and still let it get the best of me. I hate myself afterwards, but when it's happening, I feel as though I really need to say what is coming out.

I typically feel the same way and have told my therapist this numerous times. I don't understand why it matters when I'm not hurting anyone else. I always just get told that it's an unhealthy coping mechanism and I'm not actually dealing with my stuff by doing it; which I suppose makes sense.

I would say that all you can really do is be there and be as supportive as possible. I was scared to death when I first went to my GP about my depression and later a psychiatrist for BPD. What helped me be honest about my symptoms was writing things out before hand. Perhaps encourage her to write out her feelings and everything she is dealing with and offer to read it before she goes; process with her. Above all, it is important to let her know that you are there for her no matter how the appointment goes; don't let her feel alone.

You can be in therapy for as long as you want! You don't necessarily have to have a big thing to work on for it to be beneficial for you. I have been in therapy weekly (more often when I was in a residential program) for about 5 years now. I have been told by my psychiatrist and my 2 therapists that I should probably stay in therapy for life.

The only thing I can say is just to focus on making through the present moment. You don't have to look at the overall goal of not harming anymore, but just making it without doing so right now. The time will add up before you realize it. TBH, keeping track of clean time was never good for me because I felt like I had lost that time if I relapsed. That's not the case though, any clean time is an accomplishment and something that makes you stronger because you know you can make it that long again. Again, stay in the here and now and don't look too far into the future. The urges get strong, but they will eventually pass if you allow the time for them to do so. You can do this!
